1: # Entire CLI
2: 
3: Entire hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions as you work. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written in your repo.
4: 
5: With Entire, you can:
6: 
7: - **Understand why code changed** — see the full prompt/response transcript and files touched
8: - **Recover instantly** — rewind to a known-good checkpoint when an agent goes sideways and resume seamlessly
9: - **Keep Git history clean** — preserve agent context on a separate branch
10: - **Onboard faster** — show the path from prompt → change → commit
11: - **Maintain traceability** — support audit and compliance requirements when needed
12: 
13: ## Why Entire
14: 
15: - **Understand why code changed, not just what** — Transcripts, prompts, files touched, token usage, tool calls, and more are captured alongside every commit.
16: - **Rewind and resume from any checkpoint** — Go back to any previous agent session and pick up exactly where you or a coworker left off.
17: - **Full context preserved and searchable** — A versioned record of every AI interaction tied to your git history, with nothing lost.
18: - **Zero context switching** — Git-native, two-step setup, works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, and more.
19: 
20: ## Table of Contents
21: 
22: - [Why Entire](#why-entire)
23: - [Quick Start](#quick-start)
24: - [Typical Workflow](#typical-workflow)
25: - [Key Concepts](#key-concepts)
26:   - [How It Works](#how-it-works)
27:   - [Strategy](#strategy)
28: - [Local Device Auth Testing](#local-device-auth-testing)
29: - [Commands Reference](#commands-reference)
30: - [Configuration](#configuration)
31: - [Security & Privacy](#security--privacy)
32: - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
33: - [Development](#development)
34: - [Getting Help](#getting-help)
35: - [License](#license)
36: 
37: ## Requirements
38: 
39: - Git
40: - macOS, Linux or Windows
41: - [Supported agent](#agent-hook-configuration) installed and authenticated
42: 
43: ## Quick Start
44: 
45: ```bash
46: # Install stable via Homebrew
47: brew tap entireio/tap
48: brew install --cask entire
49: 
50: # Or install nightly via Homebrew
51: brew tap entireio/tap
52: brew install --cask entire@nightly
53: 
54: # Or install stable via install.sh
55: curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
56: 
57: # Or install nightly via install.sh
58: curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
59: 
60: # Or install stable via Scoop (Windows)
61: scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
62: scoop install entire/cli
63: 
64: # Or install via Go (development/manual setup)
65: go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest
66: 
67: # Linux: Add Go binaries to PATH (add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc if not already configured)
68: export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
69: 
70: # Enable in your project
71: cd your-project && entire enable
72: 
73: # Check status
74: entire status
75: ```
76: 
77: After the initial setup, use `entire agent` to add or remove agents, `entire configure` to update non-agent settings, and `entire enable` / `entire disable` to toggle Entire on or off.
78: 
79: ## Release Channels
80: 
81: Entire currently ships two release channels:
82: 
83: - `stable`: recommended for most users. Stable releases change less often and are the default for Homebrew, Scoop, and `install.sh`.
84: - `nightly`: prerelease builds for users who want the latest changes earlier. Nightlies are published more frequently and may include newer, less-proven changes than stable.
85: 
86: How to use each channel:
87: 
88: - Homebrew stable: `brew install --cask entire`
89: - Homebrew nightly: `brew install --cask entire@nightly`
90: - `install.sh` stable: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
91: - `install.sh` nightly: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly`
92: - Scoop: currently supports `stable` only via `scoop install entire/cli`
93: 
94: ## Typical Workflow
95: 
96: ### 1. Enable Entire in Your Repository
97: 
98: ```
99: entire enable
100: ```
101: 
102: On a repo that has not been enabled yet, `entire enable` runs the initial enable flow: it creates Entire settings, installs git hooks, and prompts you to choose which agent hooks to install. To enable a specific agent non-interactively, use `entire enable --agent <name>` (for example, `entire enable --agent cursor`).
103: 
104: After setup:
105: 
106: - Use `entire enable` to turn Entire back on if the repo is currently disabled.
107: - Use `entire agent` to add or remove agents.
108: - Use `entire configure` to update non-agent settings (telemetry, hooks, checkpoint remote, summary provider).
109: 
110: The hooks capture session data as you work. Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit. Your code commits stay clean, Entire never creates commits on your active branch. All session metadata is stored on a separate `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
111: 
112: ### 2. Work with Your AI Agent
113: 
114: Just use one of your AI agents as before. Entire runs in the background, tracking your session:
115: 
116: ```
117: entire status  # Check current session status anytime
118: ```
119: 
120: ### 3. Rewind to a Previous Checkpoint
121: 
122: If you want to undo some changes and go back to an earlier checkpoint:
123: 
124: ```
125: entire checkpoint rewind
126: ```
127: 
128: This shows all available checkpoints in the current session. Select one to restore your code to that exact state.
129: 
130: ### 4. Resume a Previous Session
131: 
132: To restore the latest checkpointed session metadata for a branch:
133: 
134: ```
135: entire session resume <branch>
136: ```
137: 
138: Entire checks out the branch, restores the latest checkpointed session metadata (one or more sessions), and prints command(s) to continue.
139: 
140: ### 5. Disable Entire (Optional)
141: 
142: ```
143: entire disable
144: ```
145: 
146: Removes the git hooks. Your code and commit history remain untouched.
147: 
148: ## Key Concepts
149: 
150: ### Sessions
151: 
152: A **session** represents a complete interaction with your AI agent, from start to finish. Each session captures all prompts, responses, files modified, and timestamps.
153: 
154: **Session ID format:** `YYYY-MM-DD-<UUID>` (e.g., `2026-01-08-abc123de-f456-7890-abcd-ef1234567890`)
155: 
156: Sessions are stored separately from your code commits on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
157: 
158: ### Checkpoints
159: 
160: A **checkpoint** is a snapshot within a session that you can rewind to—a "save point" in your work.
161: 
162: Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit. **Checkpoint IDs** are 12-character hex strings (e.g., `a3b2c4d5e6f7`).
163: 
164: ### How It Works
165: 
166: ```
167: Your Branch                    entire/checkpoints/v1
168:      │                                  │
169:      ▼                                  │
170: [Base Commit]                           │
171:      │                                  │
172:      │  ┌─── Agent works ───┐           │
173:      │  │  Step 1           │           │
174:      │  │  Step 2           │           │
175:      │  │  Step 3           │           │
176:      │  └───────────────────┘           │
177:      │                                  │
178:      ▼                                  ▼
179: [Your Commit] ─────────────────► [Session Metadata]
180:      │                           (transcript, prompts,
181:      │                            files touched)
182:      ▼
183: ```
184: 
185: Checkpoints are saved as you work. When you commit, session metadata is permanently stored on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch and linked to your commit.
186: 
187: ### Strategy
188: 
189: Entire uses a manual-commit strategy that keeps your git history clean:
190: 
191: - **No commits on your branch** — Entire never creates commits on the active branch
192: - **Safe on any branch** — works on main, master, and feature branches alike
193: - **Non-destructive rewind** — restore files from any checkpoint without altering commit history
194: - **Metadata stored separately** — all session data lives on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch
195: 
196: ### Git Worktrees
197: 
198: Entire works seamlessly with [git worktrees](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree). Each worktree has independent session tracking, so you can run multiple AI sessions in different worktrees without conflicts.
199: 
200: ### Concurrent Sessions
201: 
202: Multiple AI sessions can run on the same commit. If you start a second session while another has uncommitted work, Entire warns you and tracks them separately. Both sessions' checkpoints are preserved and can be rewound independently.
203: 
204: ## Local Device Auth Testing
205: 
206: If you're working on the CLI device auth flow against a local `entire.io` checkout:
207: 
208: ```bash
209: # In your app repo
210: cd ../entire.io-1
211: mise run dev
212: 
213: # In this repo, point the CLI at the local API. Both env vars are
214: # required: ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL no longer inherits from
215: # ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL — without it, the login flow reaches for the
216: # production us.auth.entire.io.
217: cd ../cli
218: export ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787
219: export ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787
220: 
221: # Run the smoke test
222: ./scripts/local-device-auth-smoke.sh
223: ```
224: 
225: Useful commands while developing:
226: 
227: ```bash
228: # Run the login flow against a local server (prompts to press Enter before opening the browser)
229: go run ./cmd/entire login --insecure-http-auth
230: 
231: # Run the focused integration coverage for login
232: go test -tags=integration ./cmd/entire/cli/integration_test -run TestLogin
233: ```

235: ## Commands Reference
236: 
237: | Command          | Description                                                                                       |
238: | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
239: | `entire clean`   | Clean up session data and orphaned Entire data (use `--all` for repo-wide cleanup)                |
240: | `entire agent`   | Add, remove, or list agent integrations for the current repository                                |
241: | `entire configure` | Update non-agent settings (telemetry, git hook, strategy options, summary provider)            |
242: | `entire disable` | Remove Entire hooks from repository                                                               |
243: | `entire doctor`  | Fix or clean up stuck sessions                                                                    |
244: | `entire enable`  | Enable Entire in your repository                                                                  |
245: | `entire checkpoint`        | List, explain, rewind, and search checkpoints                                           |
246: | `entire checkpoint explain` | Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint                                               |
247: | `entire checkpoint rewind` | Rewind to a previous checkpoint                                                         |
248: | `entire login`   | Authenticate the CLI with Entire device auth                                                      |
249: | `entire session` | View and manage agent sessions tracked by Entire                                                  |
250: | `entire session resume`    | Switch to a branch, restore latest checkpointed session metadata, and show command(s) |
251: | `entire session attach`    | Attach to a previously detached session                                                |
252: | `entire status`  | Show current session info                                                                         |
253: | `entire doctor trace` | Show hook performance traces                                                                 |
254: | `entire version` | Show Entire CLI version                                                                           |
255: 
256: ### `entire enable` Flags
257: 
258: | Flag                                        | Description                                                                                                       |
259: | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
260: | `--agent <name>`                            | AI agent to install hooks for: `claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, or `copilot-cli` |
261: | `--force`, `-f`                             | Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)                                                       |
262: | `--local`                                   | Write settings to `settings.local.json` instead of `settings.json`                                                |
263: | `--project`                                 | Write settings to `settings.json` even if it already exists                                                       |
264: | `--skip-push-sessions`                      | Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push                                                             |
265: | `--checkpoint-remote <provider:owner/repo>` | Push checkpoint branches to a separate repo (e.g., `github:org/checkpoints-repo`)                                 |
266: | `--telemetry=false`                         | Disable anonymous usage analytics                                                                                 |
267: 
268: **Examples:**
269: 
270: ```
271: # First-time setup with a specific agent
272: entire enable --agent claude-code
273: 
274: # Re-enable a disabled repo
275: entire enable
276: 
277: # Re-enable and refresh hooks
278: entire enable --force
279: 
280: # Save settings locally (not committed to git)
281: entire enable --local
282: ```
283: 
284: `entire enable` is primarily for turning Entire on. On an unconfigured repo it will also bootstrap setup. Use `entire agent` for adding or removing agents, and `entire configure` for non-agent settings.
285: 
286: ### `entire configure`
287: 
288: Use `entire configure` to update non-agent settings on a repo that's already set up. Agent installation lives under `entire agent`.
289: 
290: Typical uses:
291: 
292: - Toggle telemetry
293: - Reinstall the Entire git hook (`--force`, `--absolute-git-hook-path`)
294: - Update strategy options such as `--checkpoint-remote` or `--skip-push-sessions`
295: - Pick a summary provider for `entire explain --generate`
296: 
297: **Examples:**
298: 
299: ```bash
300: # Show help and the hint pointing to 'entire agent'
301: entire configure
302: 
303: # Opt out of telemetry
304: entire configure --telemetry=false
305: 
306: # Reinstall the Entire git hook with an absolute binary path
307: entire configure --absolute-git-hook-path
308: 
309: # Update strategy options on an existing repo
310: entire configure --checkpoint-remote github:myorg/checkpoints-private
311: 
312: # Add or remove an agent
313: entire agent add claude-code
314: entire agent remove claude-code
315: ```
316: 
317: ## Configuration
318: 
319: Entire uses two configuration files in the `.entire/` directory:
320: 
321: ### settings.json (Project Settings)
322: 
323: Shared across the team, typically committed to git:
324: 
325: ```json
326: {
327:   "enabled": true
328: }
329: ```
330: 
331: ### settings.local.json (Local Settings)
332: 
333: Personal overrides, gitignored by default:
334: 
335: ```json
336: {
337:   "enabled": false,
338:   "log_level": "debug"
339: }
340: ```
341: 
342: ### Configuration Options
343: 
344: | Option                               | Values                                       | Description                                             |
345: | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
346: | `enabled`                            | `true`, `false`                              | Enable/disable Entire                                   |
347: | `log_level`                          | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`             | Logging verbosity                                       |
348: | `strategy_options.push_sessions`     | `true`, `false`                              | Auto-push `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch on git push    |
349: | `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote` | `{"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"}` | Push checkpoint branches to a separate repo (see below) |
350: | `strategy_options.summarize.enabled` | `true`, `false`                              | Auto-generate AI summaries at commit time               |
351: | `telemetry`                          | `true`, `false`                              | Send anonymous usage statistics to Posthog              |
352: 
353: ### Agent Hook Configuration
354: 
355: Each agent stores its hook configuration in its own directory. When you run `entire enable`, hooks are installed in the appropriate location for each selected agent:
356: 
357: | Agent            | Hook Location                 | Format            |
358: | ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------- |
359: | Claude Code      | `.claude/settings.json`       | JSON hooks config |
360: | Codex            | `.codex/hooks.json`           | JSON hooks config |
361: | Copilot CLI      | `.github/hooks/entire.json`   | JSON hooks config |
362: | Cursor           | `.cursor/hooks.json`          | JSON hooks config |
363: | Factory AI Droid | `.factory/settings.json`      | JSON hooks config |
364: | Gemini CLI       | `.gemini/settings.json`       | JSON hooks config |
365: | OpenCode         | `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` | TypeScript plugin |
366: | Pi               | `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` | TypeScript extension |
367: 
368: You can enable multiple agents at the same time — each agent's hooks are independent. Entire detects which agents are active by checking for installed hooks, not by a setting in `settings.json`.
369: 
370: ### Checkpoint Remote
371: 
372: By default, Entire pushes `entire/checkpoints/v1` to the same remote as your code. If you want to push checkpoint data to a separate repo (e.g., a private repo for public projects), configure `checkpoint_remote` with a structured provider and repo:
373: 
374: ```json
375: {
376:   "strategy_options": {
377:     "checkpoint_remote": {
378:       "provider": "github",
379:       "repo": "myorg/checkpoints-private"
380:     }
381:   }
382: }
383: ```
384: 
385: Or via the CLI:
386: 
387: ```bash
388: entire enable --checkpoint-remote github:myorg/checkpoints-private
389: ```
390: 
391: Entire derives the git URL automatically using the same protocol (SSH or HTTPS) as your push remote. It will:
392: 
393: - Fetch the checkpoint branch locally if it exists on the remote but not locally (one-time)
394: - Push `entire/checkpoints/v1` to the checkpoint repo instead of your default push remote
395: - Skip pushing if a fork is detected (push remote owner differs from checkpoint repo owner)
396: - If the remote is unreachable, warn and continue without blocking your main push
397: 
398: #### `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`
399: 
400: `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` allows you to provide a dedicated token for checkpoint repository operations, without modifying the credentials used for your primary repository.
401: 
402: When this environment variable is set, Entire behaves as follows:
403: 
404: - Injects the token into HTTPS Git operations used for checkpoint fetch and push
405: - If `checkpoint_remote` is configured:
406:   - Prefers an HTTPS URL for the checkpoint remote when a token is present, even if the repository’s `origin` uses SSH
407: - If `checkpoint_remote` is not configured:
408:   - Falls back to using the default `origin` remote
409: - If `checkpoint_remote` configuration cannot be loaded:
410:   - Falls back to `origin`
411:   - If `origin` is a valid SSH or HTTPS Git remote, Entire converts it to an HTTPS URL to enable token-based authentication
412: 
413: ### Auto-Summarization
414: 
415: When enabled, Entire automatically generates AI summaries for checkpoints at commit time. Summaries capture intent, outcome, learnings, friction points, and open items from the session.
416: 
417: ```json
418: {
419:   "strategy_options": {
420:     "summarize": {
421:       "enabled": true
422:     }
423:   }
424: }
425: ```
426: 
427: **Requirements:**
428: 
429: - Claude CLI must be installed and authenticated (`claude` command available in PATH)
430: - Summary generation is non-blocking: failures are logged but don't prevent commits
431: 
432: **Note:** Currently uses Claude CLI for summary generation. Other AI backends may be supported in future versions.
433: 
434: ### Settings Priority
435: 
436: Local settings override project settings field-by-field. When you run `entire status`, it shows both project and local (effective) settings.
437: 
438: ### Agent-Specific Steps & Limitations
439: 
440: - When enabling Entire for Codex, the command will also create or update `.codex/config.toml` with `codex_hooks = true` to enable Codex hooks. If you configure Codex manually, make sure this flag is set in your `.codex/config.toml`. Or select Codex from the interactive agent picker when running `entire enable`.
441: - Entire supports Cursor IDE and Cursor Agent CLI tool, but `entire rewind` is not available at this time. Other commands (`doctor`, `status` etc.) work the same as all other agents.
442: - Entire supports Copilot CLI, but not Copilot in VS Code, in other IDEs, or on github.com.
443: - Entire supports Pi coding agent (Preview). Pi uses a TypeScript extension instead of a JSON hook config. Subagent capture is not currently available.
444: 
445: ## Security & Privacy
446: 
447: **Your session transcripts are stored in your git repository** on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. If your repository is public, this data is visible to anyone.
448: 
449: Entire automatically redacts detected secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) when writing to `entire/checkpoints/v1`, but redaction is best-effort. Temporary shadow branches used during a session may contain unredacted data and should not be pushed. See [docs/security-and-privacy.md](docs/security-and-privacy.md) for details.
450: 
451: ## Troubleshooting
452: 
453: ### Common Issues
454: 
455: | Issue                    | Solution                                                |
456: | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
457: | "Not a git repository"   | Navigate to a Git repository first                      |
458: | "Entire is disabled"     | Run `entire enable`                                     |
459: | "No rewind points found" | Work with your configured agent and commit your changes |
460: | "shadow branch conflict" | Run `entire clean --force`                              |
461: 
462: ### SSH Authentication Errors
463: 
464: If you see an error like this when running `entire resume`:
465: 
466: ```
467: Failed to fetch metadata: failed to fetch entire/checkpoints/v1 from origin: ssh: handshake failed: ssh: unable to authenticate, attempted methods [none publickey], no supported methods remain

package paths

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

// GetWorktreeID returns the internal git worktree identifier for the given path.
// For the main worktree (where .git is a directory), returns empty string.
// For linked worktrees (where .git is a file), extracts the name from
// .git/worktrees/<name>/ path. This name is stable across `git worktree move`.
func GetWorktreeID(worktreePath string) (string, error) {
	gitPath := filepath.Join(worktreePath, ".git")

	info, err := os.Stat(gitPath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to stat .git: %w", err)
	}

	// Main worktree has .git as a directory
	if info.IsDir() {
		return "", nil
	}

	// Linked worktree has .git as a file with content: "gitdir: /path/to/.git/worktrees/<name>"
	content, err := os.ReadFile(gitPath) //nolint:gosec // gitPath is constructed from worktreePath + ".git"
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to read .git file: %w", err)
	}

	line := strings.TrimSpace(string(content))
	if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "gitdir: ") {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid .git file format: %s", line)
	}

	gitdir := strings.TrimPrefix(line, "gitdir: ")

	// Extract worktree name from path like /repo/.git/worktrees/<name>
	// or /repo/.bare/worktrees/<name> (bare repo + worktree layout).
	// The path after the marker is the worktree identifier.
	var worktreeID string
	var found bool
	for _, marker := range []string{".git/worktrees/", ".bare/worktrees/"} {
		_, worktreeID, found = strings.Cut(gitdir, marker)
		if found {
			break
		}
	}
	if !found {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected gitdir format (no worktrees): %s", gitdir)
	}
	// Remove trailing slashes if any
	worktreeID = strings.TrimSuffix(worktreeID, "/")

	return worktreeID, nil
}
```

## Bug Analysis

### Bug 1 (Primary, Known Issue #640): Submodule gitdirs cause `GetWorktreeID` to error out

**Severity:** Critical -- blocks session initialization entirely in git submodules

**Root cause:** The function assumes that any `.git` *file* (as opposed to a directory) is a linked worktree pointer. It then searches the gitdir path for `.git/worktrees/` or `.bare/worktrees/` and returns an error if neither marker is found.

**What happens with submodules:** A git submodule's `.git` file contains a path like:

```
gitdir: ../../.git/modules/go-git
```

or

```
gitdir: /absolute/path/.git/modules/deps/go-git
```

These paths contain `.git/modules/` but NOT `.git/worktrees/` or `.bare/worktrees/`. The `strings.Cut` loop finds no marker, `found` stays `false`, and the function returns:

```
unexpected gitdir format (no worktrees): ../../.git/modules/go-git

**Severity:** High -- shadow branch name collision or corruption

**Scenario:** When a submodule is checked out inside a linked worktree of the superproject, the submodule's `.git` file can look like:

```
gitdir: /super/.git/worktrees/super-linked/modules/deps/go-git
```

The current parsing logic uses `strings.Cut(gitdir, ".git/worktrees/")`, which finds the `.git/worktrees/` marker and returns everything after it:

```
super-linked/modules/deps/go-git
```

But `super-linked` is the superproject's linked worktree ID, not the submodule's. The submodule is the main worktree of the submodule repository and should return `""`.

**Severity:** Medium -- rare but real edge case

**Scenario:** A submodule repository itself can have a linked worktree. In that case, the `.git` file would contain:

```
gitdir: /super/.git/modules/deps/go-git/worktrees/sub-linked
```

```
sub-linked   (correct by accident in this specific case)
```

The `strings.Cut` searches for `.git/worktrees/` and finds it at the `/super/.git/worktrees/` position... except this path does NOT contain `.git/worktrees/` -- it contains `.git/modules/deps/go-git/worktrees/sub-linked`. It would NOT find `.git/worktrees/` because the actual pattern is `go-git/worktrees/` not `.git/worktrees/`. So it would fall through to `.bare/worktrees/`, also not find it, and return an error.

**This is actually a distinct bug:** The function cannot parse a submodule's own linked worktree and would return an error instead of the worktree ID `sub-linked`.

---

**Severity:** Low -- the `before` return value is unused but confusing

**Detail:** On line 46, `strings.Cut(gitdir, marker)` returns three values: `(before, after, found)`. The `before` value (the part before the marker) is discarded with `_`. This is correct behavior for the current use case, but it's worth noting that `strings.Cut` finds the *first* occurrence of the marker. If the gitdir path somehow contained the marker twice (e.g., a deeply nested scenario), only the first occurrence would be split on.

This is not currently exploitable because the markers `.git/worktrees/` and `.bare/worktrees/` are unlikely to appear twice, but it relates to the false-positive issue in Bug 2.

---

### Bug 5 (Minor): `strings.TrimSuffix(worktreeID, "/")` only removes a single trailing slash

**Severity:** Very low -- unlikely in practice

If a gitdir path ends with multiple slashes (e.g., due to some unusual configuration or corruption), only one would be removed. Using `strings.TrimRight(worktreeID, "/")` would be more defensive. This is extremely unlikely in practice since git itself doesn't produce such paths.

---

### Bug 6 (Edge Case): Multiline `.git` files not handled

**Severity:** Very low -- git does not produce multiline `.git` files in practice

`strings.TrimSpace` on line 33 will collapse the entire file content into a single line. If a `.git` file ever contained extra lines (it shouldn't in normal git operation), only the first line (which contains the `gitdir:` directive) would be relevant, but `TrimSpace` would join any subsequent lines into the string, causing `strings.HasPrefix(line, "gitdir: ")` to still match but `strings.TrimPrefix` would leave trailing content. Here's a comprehensive bug report, organized by severity:

---

## CRITICAL — Session-Blocking Bugs

### 1. `GetWorktreeID` rejects submodules entirely (Issue #640)
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/paths/worktree.go:51`

Git submodules have `.git` files pointing to `.git/modules/<name>` (not `.git/worktrees/`). The function errors with `"unexpected gitdir format (no worktrees)"`, **blocking all session initialization in submodule checkouts**.

### 2. `GetWorktreeID` returns wrong worktree ID for submodule inside linked superproject worktree
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/paths/worktree.go:46`

For a submodule inside a linked superproject worktree, the `.git` file contains something like `gitdir: /repo/.git/worktrees/feature/modules/deps`. `strings.Cut(gitdir, ".git/worktrees/")` incorrectly matches the superproject's worktree ID, returning `"feature/modules/deps"` instead of `""`.

### 3. `GetWorktreeID` cannot parse submodule's own linked worktree
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/paths/worktree.go:46`

A submodule's own linked worktree has gitdir like `gitdir: /repo/.git/modules/deps/worktrees/sub-wt`. The `.git/worktrees/` marker is not present (it's `modules/deps/worktrees/`), so the function errors instead of returning `"sub-wt"`.

---

## HIGH — Runtime Panics & Data Issues

### 4. Panic on short checkpoint IDs in non-interactive rewind
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/rewind.go:556`

```go
selectedPoint.ID[:7]  // panics if ID < 7 chars
```

The interactive flow at line 204 correctly guards with `if len(shortID) > 7`, but the non-interactive flow at line 556 slices unconditionally. Short IDs would cause an index-out-of-range panic.

### 5. Empty session ID falls back to literal `"unknown"`, risking collisions
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:465-468`

When `event.SessionID` is empty, the code assigns `sessionID = "unknown"`. This creates directories like `.entire/sessions/unknown/` and shadow branches that collide across different sessions missing their IDs.

### 6. `filepath.Base("")` produces `"."` as session ID in rewind
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/rewind.go:320`

When `selectedPoint.SessionID` is empty AND `selectedPoint.MetadataDir` is empty, `filepath.Base("")` returns `"."`, producing bogus transcript paths.

---

## MEDIUM — Functional Bugs

### 7. `d.Name()` drops subdirectory paths in `listAllTempFiles`
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/clean.go:436,443`

```go
fs.WalkDir(root.FS(), ".", func(_ string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
    ...
    files = append(files, d.Name())  // should use path, not d.Name()
```

`WalkDir` provides the full relative path as the first argument, but it's discarded. `d.Name()` only returns the base filename, so files in subdirectories of `.entire/tmp/` cannot be deleted.

### 8. TOCTOU race on `prompt.txt` read-then-write during concurrent TurnStart
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:382-400`

Two concurrent TurnStart hooks for the same session can read the same existing `prompt.txt`, then both write their version, causing one prompt to be lost.

### 9. `normalizeToolUsePaths` silently drops files when `eventCWD` is relative
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:337`

If an agent provides a relative `eventCWD`, `filepath.Join(eventCWD, f)` produces a non-absolute path that `FilterAndNormalizePaths` then rejects (returns `""`), silently dropping those files from tracking.

### 10. `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` hard-fails on `WorktreeRoot` error
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:931-933`

Unlike `handleLifecycleToolUse` which gracefully degrades, this handler returns a hard error if `WorktreeRoot()` fails, blocking all subagent processing in edge cases (e.g., submodule worktrees).

### 11. `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` resolves empty `SessionRef` to CWD-relative path
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:871`

`filepath.Dir("")` returns `"."`, so an empty `SessionRef` produces `AgentTranscriptPath(".", subagentID)` — a relative path resolved against CWD, not repo root.

### 12. `GetMainRepoRoot` doesn't handle submodule `.git` file format
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:1026-1053`

For submodules, the gitdir path is relative and contains `.git/modules/` instead of `.git/worktrees/`. `strings.LastIndex(gitdir, "/.git/")` produces an incorrect parent directory.

### 13. `goroutineID()` collision risk in `acquireSessionGate`
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_state.go:489-537`

If `goroutineID()` returns `-1` for two different goroutines (e.g., if `runtime.Stack` parsing fails), they'd see `gate.owner == -1` and treat each other as the same goroutine, causing one goroutine's mutations to be silently skipped.

### 14. `DeleteOrphanedCheckpoints` creates unsigned commits
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/cleanup.go:244-338`

Unlike `EnsureMetadataBranch` and condensation code which call `checkpoint.SignCommitBestEffort()`, this function creates unsigned commits on `entire/checkpoints/v1`. On repos enforcing commit signature verification, pushes would be rejected.

---

## LOW — Minor / Edge Cases

### 15. `formatRelativeDuration` returns `"just now"` for negative durations
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/status.go:237-248`
Negative `time.Since()` (from future timestamps/clock skew) falls into `d < time.Minute` and returns "just now".

### 16. `saveEnabledState` asymmetry in settings sync
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:1141-1158`
When saving to local settings, the project settings file is NOT updated, so a conflicting `enabled` field in project settings can override the local value.

### 17. `performGitResetHard` only validates leading `-`
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/rewind.go:1173-1182`
Only checks for leading dash, doesn't validate that the commit hash is purely hex. (Defense-in-depth: `exec.Command` prevents shell injection.)

### 18. `protectedDirs()` cache has no test-facing reset function
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:362-373`
A comment mentions `resetProtectedDirsForTest()` but it doesn't exist, so tests that mutate the agent registry after the first call see stale results.

### 19. `Rewind` doesn't skip submodule entries in checkpoint tree
**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go:402-440`
Iterating over tree files that include submodule entries (mode `160000`) would fail when trying `f.Contents()` since submodules are commit references, not blobs.

## Bug #1: `GetWorktreeID` rejects submodules entirely (Issue #640)

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/paths/worktree.go:51`

This is the bug this branch is named after. Let me explain the full chain:

**How it fails:**

```
1. You run `entire enable` inside a repo that has a submodule
2. An agent hook fires inside the submodule checkout
3. The hook calls InitializeSession → which calls GetWorktreeID
4. GetWorktreeID reads the submodule's .git file:
     gitdir: ../../.git/modules/go-git
5. It searches for ".git/worktrees/" or ".bare/worktrees/"
6. Neither is found → returns error: "unexpected gitdir format (no worktrees)"
7. Session initialization ABORTS. Entire is completely broken in this submodule.
```

**Why it happens:** The function assumes any `.git` *file* (as opposed to directory) is a linked worktree pointer. But git submodules also use `.git` files — they just point to `.git/modules/<name>` instead of `.git/worktrees/<id>`.

**The correct behavior:** An ordinary submodule checkout is the main worktree of the submodule repository. It should return `""` (empty string), just like a regular main worktree where `.git` is a directory.
